---
params:
  x:
  tab_title:
  type:
  meta: !r NULL
  cohort: !r NULL
title: "Basistabelle `r params$tab_title`"
subtitle: "`r paste0(if(params$type == 'dq') 'nach Mitteldurchmesser-Klassen' else 'nach Altersklassen', if (identical(params$cohort, 'mainstand')) ', Hauptbestand' else if (identical(params$cohort, 'alllayers')) ', Alle Schichten' else paste0(', Benutzerdefinierte Auswahl: ', params$cohort))`"
classoption:
  - a4paper
geometry:
  - portrait
  - "left=0.7cm,right=0.7cm,top=1cm,bottom=1.2cm"
fontsize: 10pt
header-includes:
  # The table LaTeX is emitted via cat() from an asis chunk (to post-process
  # the page-break behaviour), so knitr does not auto-load the kableExtra table
  # packages -- declare them here.
  - \usepackage{booktabs}
  - \usepackage{longtable}
  - \usepackage{array}
---
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r meta-block, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(params$meta)) {
  m <- params$meta
  # Thousands separated by a space, not a dot: "15 575" reads the same to
  # German and English readers, whereas "15.575" looks like a decimal number.
  fmt_ha <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = " ", decimal.mark = ",",
                                scientific = FALSE)
  parts <- character(0)
  if (!is.null(m$year))    parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Inventurjahr:} ",       as.integer(m$year)))
  if (!is.null(m$area_ha)) parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Gesamtfl\\\"ache:} ",  fmt_ha(m$area_ha), " ha"))
  if (!is.null(m$n_plots)) parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Inventurpunkte:} ",    as.integer(m$n_plots)))
  if (length(parts) > 0)
    cat("\\begin{center}\\small ", paste(parts, collapse = "\\qquad "), "\\end{center}\\vspace{-0.5em}\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "asis"}

# https://haozhu233.github.io/kableExtra/awesome_table_in_html.html
# https://www.pipinghotdata.com/posts/2022-01-24-report-ready-pdf-tables-with-rmarkdown-knitr-kableextra-and-latex/

oo <- options(knitr.kable.NA = "", fe_spec_lang = "ger")

# Take the table from params, not from the calling frame. rmarkdown::render()
# evaluates in the caller's environment, so a bare `x` happened to resolve to
# the local variable of output_base_table_pdf() - which only works as long as
# that argument keeps its name. Everything below then works on this local copy.
x <- params$x

# Prevent page breaks WITHIN a species block of a kableExtra longtable (same
# mechanism as the increment base tables). Each pack_rows group starts with a
# line "\addlinespace[0.3em]". A longtable row ending in "\\" allows a break
# after it, "\\*" forbids it. We turn every breakable terminator into "\\*",
# except the row right before the next group boundary, so breaks still happen
# between species blocks. Blocks are small (a handful of rows), so they never
# exceed a page.
no_break_within_groups <- function(tex) {
  lines <- strsplit(tex, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  is_boundary <- trimws(lines) == "\\addlinespace[0.3em]"
  n <- length(lines)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    ln <- lines[i]
    if (endsWith(ln, "\\\\") && !endsWith(ln, "\\\\*")) {
      j <- i + 1L
      while (j <= n && trimws(lines[j]) == "") j <- j + 1L
      next_boundary <- j <= n && is_boundary[j]
      next_end      <- j <= n && grepl("end{longtable}", lines[j], fixed = TRUE)
      if (!next_boundary && !next_end) lines[i] <- paste0(ln, "*")
    }
  }
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

# 1. Filter and translate BEFORE building row-count index.
# The two G-share rows: pct_anteil_bag is the species group's basal-area share
# within its (age/dq) class column (columns sum to 100 % across species);
# pct_anteil_class is the class' basal-area share of the grand total (the
# Gesamt block, rows sum to 100 % across classes). Both are labelled "G-Ant."
# and disambiguated by a footnote. conf_95_per is the +/- half-width of the
# 95 % confidence interval of V, in percent of V.
x <- x |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variable != "tot_area_class") |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = dplyr::recode(.data$variable,
    v_hub_m3    = "V (m³)",
    g_m2        = "G (m²)",
    n           = "N",
    d_q_cm      = "dg (cm)",
    h_q_m       = "hg (m)",
    n_plot      = "Anz. Pkte.",
    area_ha     = "Fl. ideell (ha)",
    v_hub_m3_ha = "V (m³/ha)",
    g_m2_ha     = "G (m²/ha)",
    n_ha        = "N (/ha)",
    conf_95_per = "95%-VB (± %)",
    pct_anteil_bag   = "G-Ant. Artgr. (%)",
    pct_anteil_class = "G-Ant. Klasse (%)"
  ))

# 1a. The area share needs a label that depends on the block it sits in,
# because one variable carries two meanings (unlike the basal-area shares,
# which arrive as two separate variables): inside a species block per_species
# is the species group's share of the class column's ideal area (columns sum
# to 100 %), whereas in the cross-species block it is the class' share of the
# total ideal area (the row sums to 100 %). The names mirror the two G-share
# rows so the parallel is visible.
x <- x |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = dplyr::case_when(
    .data$variable != "per_species"  ~ .data$variable,
    is.na(.data$species_group)       ~ "Fl.-Ant. Klasse (%)",
    TRUE                             ~ "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)"
  ))

# 1b. Row order within each species block: an annotation row sits directly
# under the quantity it belongs to - the 95 % CI under V, the G-share rows
# under G - and "Anz. Pkte." always comes last. Absent rows (e.g. the per-ha
# / area rows exist only in the main-stand variant) are simply skipped.
.var_order <- c("V (m³)", "95%-VB (± %)", "G (m²)", "G-Ant. Artgr. (%)",
                "G-Ant. Klasse (%)", "N", "dg (cm)", "hg (m)",
                "Fl. ideell (ha)", "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)", "Fl.-Ant. Klasse (%)",
                "V (m³/ha)", "G (m²/ha)", "N (/ha)",
                "Anz. Pkte.")
x <- x |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = factor(.data$variable, levels = .var_order,
                                  ordered = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(is.na(.data$species_group), .data$species_group,
                 .data$variable) |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = as.character(.data$variable))

# 2. Vertical grouping by species (must reflect filtered row count).
#    The cross-species block carries a NA species_group; it is forced to the
#    bottom and labelled "Alle Artgruppen" - distinct from the "Gesamt" column
#    on the right (the species rows keep their original order).
vertical_index_dat <- x |>
  dplyr::group_by(species_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(is.na(species_group), species_group)

vertical_index <- vertical_index_dat$n
grp_names <- format(vertical_index_dat$species_group)
grp_names[is.na(vertical_index_dat$species_group)] <- "Alle Artgruppen"
names(vertical_index) <- grp_names

# 3. Drop species_group column and rename variable/total columns
x <- x |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-"species_group") |>
  dplyr::rename("Artgruppe" = "variable", "Gesamt" = "total")

# 3b. dg and hg are suppressed in the "Gesamt" column. That column pools every
# class of the block, and the basal-area mean tree of such a wide collective
# describes no real stand any more - a single dg over all age classes from
# thicket to old timber is not a meaningful figure. The cells are blanked
# (knitr.kable.NA = "") rather than the rows dropped, so the block keeps its
# per-class values.
x$Gesamt[x$Artgruppe %in% c("dg (cm)", "hg (m)")] <- NA

# 4. Pre-format numeric columns, German conventions: decimal comma, and
# thousands separated by a space (unambiguous in both German and English,
# unlike a thousands dot, which reads as a decimal point to English readers).
# The absolute V / G / N rows and the point counts are shown as whole numbers -
# deliberately NOT rescaled to thousands, because small enterprises (e.g. 100
# ha) would lose all resolution that way. Their per-ha siblings and every other
# row keep one decimal.
fmt_de <- function(v, digits) {
  formatC(v, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = " ", decimal.mark = ",")
}
num_col_names <- names(x)[sapply(x, is.numeric)]
int_rows      <- c("V (m³)", "G (m²)", "N", "Anz. Pkte.")
is_int_row    <- x$Artgruppe %in% int_rows
for (cn in num_col_names) {
  x[[cn]] <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x[[cn]])  ~ NA_character_,
    is_int_row      ~ fmt_de(round(x[[cn]]), 0),
    TRUE            ~ fmt_de(x[[cn]], 1)
  )
}

# 5. Horizontal grouping header. The class columns are everything between the
# row-label column and "Gesamt" - counted by exclusion rather than by their
# "(a,b]" spelling, because trees of unknown age form a class column literally
# named "NA", which the spelling test would leave outside the spanner.
n_class_cols     <- ncol(x) - 2L
horizontal_index <- c(1, n_class_cols, 1)

if (params$type == "age") {
  names(horizontal_index) <- c(" ", "Altersklassen (Jahre)", " ")
} else {
  names(horizontal_index) <- c(" ", "dg-Klassen (cm)", " ")
}

# 5b. Open top class: (160,999] / (60,999] -> ">160" / ">60" (999 is the
# sentinel upper break from pulled_methods.R).
names(x) <- sub("^\\(([0-9]+),999\\]$", ">\\1", names(x))

# 5c. Trees without an age end up in a class whose level is NA, which pivots to
# a column named "NA". It gets a short label rather than a descriptive one: the
# header is what sets this column's width, and a spelt-out heading pushed wide
# tables (e.g. Sailershausen) over the page. What "k. A." stands for is
# explained in the notes below the table instead.
na_col <- names(x) == "NA"
has_no_class_col <- any(na_col)
if (has_no_class_col) names(x)[na_col] <- "k. A."

# 5d. Fit the table to the text width. The number of class columns is not fixed
# (an extra "o. Altersangabe" column appears whenever ages are incomplete) and
# neither is the magnitude of the numbers, so a large enterprise with an extra
# column can outgrow the page. A longtable cannot be scaled with \resizebox -
# it has to stay breakable across pages - so the levers are the font size and
# the inter-column padding, and both are derived from the actual content.
#
# The width of a column is estimated from its widest entry, charging 0.5 em per
# digit or letter (the width of a digit in the default font, which uses tabular
# figures) and 0.3 em for spaces and punctuation. Padding is given up before
# type size, because tighter columns are far less noticeable than smaller
# print.
#
# Everything below is derived from the page geometry and from the content of
# this particular table - no constant is tuned to any specific inventory.
page_width_cm <- 21.0   # a4paper (classoption in the YAML header)
margin_cm     <- 0.7    # keep in sync with the geometry setting above
text_width_pt <- (page_width_cm - 2 * margin_cm) / 2.54 * 72.27

str_width_em <- function(s) {
  s <- s[!is.na(s)]
  if (length(s) == 0) return(0)
  max(vapply(strsplit(s, "", fixed = TRUE), function(chs) {
    sum(ifelse(chs %in% c(" ", ".", ",", "(", ")", "%", "-"), 0.30, 0.50))
  }, numeric(1)))
}

col_em <- vapply(seq_along(x), function(j) {
  max(str_width_em(as.character(x[[j]])), str_width_em(names(x)[j]))
}, numeric(1))

font_sizes <- c(8, 7, 6, 5)
colseps    <- c(6, 4, 3, 2)
# Fallback if even the smallest combination is too wide: use it anyway, so the
# table is as narrow as this mechanism can make it.
fit   <- list(font_size = min(font_sizes), colsep = min(colseps))
found <- FALSE
for (fs in font_sizes) {
  for (cs in colseps) {
    if (sum(col_em) * fs + 2 * cs * ncol(x) <= text_width_pt) {
      fit   <- list(font_size = fs, colsep = cs)
      found <- TRUE
      break
    }
  }
  if (found) break
}

# 6. Render table. The generated LaTeX is post-processed so that a species
#    block is never split across a page boundary.
kbl <- knitr::kable(x, format = "latex",
             format.args = list(scientific = FALSE),
             booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE,
             align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(x) - 1))) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(horizontal_index) |>
  kableExtra::pack_rows(index = vertical_index,
                        hline_after = FALSE,
                        hline_before = TRUE) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = fit$font_size,
                            latex_options = c("repeat_header"))

# 6b. Set the area / per-hectare block off visually: a rule above the first of
# its rows and one below the last. Deliberately \cmidrule and not \midrule -
# \midrule spans the full tabular width like the species separators, whereas
# \cmidrule(lr){1-n} covers just the row labels and the numbers and is trimmed
# at both ends, so it reads as a subdivision inside a species block rather
# than as another block boundary. Only present in the main-stand variant,
# which is the only one carrying these rows.
bracket_block <- function(tex, first_row, last_row, n_col) {
  lines <- strsplit(tex, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  rule  <- sprintf("\\cmidrule(lr){1-%d}", n_col)
  out   <- character(0)
  for (ln in lines) {
    if (grepl(first_row, ln, fixed = TRUE)) out <- c(out, rule)
    out <- c(out, ln)
    if (grepl(last_row, ln, fixed = TRUE))  out <- c(out, rule)
  }
  paste(out, collapse = "\n")
}

tex <- no_break_within_groups(as.character(kbl))
if ("Fl. ideell (ha)" %in% x$Artgruppe && "N (/ha)" %in% x$Artgruppe)
  tex <- bracket_block(tex, "Fl. ideell (ha) &", "N (/ha) &", ncol(x))

# Emitted as a plain command (no brace group), which pandoc passes through as
# raw LaTeX; the table is the only tabular material in the document.
cat("\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{", fit$colsep, "pt}\n", sep = "")
cat(tex)

options(oo)
```

```{r disclaimer, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
disc_text <- NULL
if (identical(params$cohort, "mainstand")) {
  # The main-stand caveat mirrors the one carried by the increment base tables:
  # restricting the table to the main stand is what makes ideal (virtual pure
  # stand) species areas computable in the first place, but those areas are
  # methodically delicate, so anything derived from them needs care.
  disc_text <- paste0("Diese Tabelle umfasst nur den Hauptbestand, nicht das ",
                      "gesamte erfasste Inventurkollektiv. Nur für den ",
                      "Hauptbestand lassen sich ideelle Baumarten-Anteilsflächen ",
                      "und darauf bezogene Hektarwerte berechnen. Die Berechnung ",
                      "solcher ideellen Anteilsflächen ist aus methodischer Sicht ",
                      "allerdings problematisch; darauf bezogene Werte sind stets ",
                      "mit Vorsicht zu interpretieren.")
} else if (identical(params$cohort, "alllayers")) {
  disc_text <- paste0("Diese Tabelle beinhaltet die Werte aller Bestandesschichten. ",
                      "Sie umfasst daher das gesamte Holzvolumen des Betriebes, ",
                      "erlaubt aber nicht die Berechnung von ideellen Flächenanteilen ",
                      "und daher auch nicht die Angabe von darauf bezogenen ",
                      "Per-Hektar-Werten.")
}

# Explanatory notes below the table. Which entries appear depends on the rows
# the variant actually carries (the main-stand variant has area / per-ha rows
# the all-layers variant does not), so nothing is explained that is not shown.
vars_present <- unique(x$Artgruppe)
has <- function(v) v %in% vars_present
# "%" starts a comment in LaTeX and this block is emitted as raw LaTeX.
esc <- function(s) gsub("%", "\\\\%", s)

notes <- character(0)
if (!is.null(disc_text)) notes <- c(notes, disc_text)
notes <- c(notes,
  "Alle Volumenangaben verstehen sich als Erntefestmeter ohne Rinde (Efm o.R.).")
# Only explained when the column is actually there (it appears whenever the
# inventory carries incomplete ages).
if (has_no_class_col)
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "k. A.: keine Altersangabe. Diese Spalte fasst alle Bäume zusammen, für die ",
    "kein Alter vorliegt; sie bilden eine eigene Klasse und sind damit in den ",
    "Zeilensummen der Spalte \"Gesamt\" enthalten."))
# The confidence-interval note follows the volume note directly: it refers to
# V and belongs next to the statement of V's unit.
if (has("95%-VB (± %)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "95%-VB (± %): halbe Breite des zweiseitigen 95%-Vertrauensbereichs des ",
    "Vorrats V, in Prozent von V. Der zugrundeliegende Standardfehler ist ",
    "flächengewichtet geschätzt."))
if (has("dg (cm)") || has("hg (m)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "dg, hg: Durchmesser bzw. Höhe des Grundflächenmittelstamms. In der Spalte ",
    "\"Gesamt\" werden dg und hg nicht ausgewiesen: über alle Klassen hinweg ",
    "ist die Angabe eines Mittelstamms nicht sinnvoll."))
if (has("G-Ant. Artgr. (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "G-Ant. Artgr. (%): Grundflächenanteil der Artgruppe innerhalb der ",
    "jeweiligen Klassenspalte. Die Werte einer Spalte summieren sich über alle ",
    "Artgruppen zu 100 %."))
if (has("G-Ant. Klasse (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "G-Ant. Klasse (%): Grundflächenanteil der jeweiligen Klasse am Gesamtwert. ",
    "Die Werte dieser Zeile summieren sich über alle Klassen zu 100 %."))
if (has("Fl. ideell (ha)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl. ideell (ha): ideelle Anteilsfläche der Artgruppe; die hektarbezogenen ",
    "Werte beziehen sich auf diese Fläche."))
if (has("Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%): Anteil der Artgruppe an der ideellen Fläche der ",
    "jeweiligen Klassenspalte. Die Werte einer Spalte summieren sich über alle ",
    "Artgruppen zu 100 %."))
if (has("Fl.-Ant. Klasse (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl.-Ant. Klasse (%): Anteil der jeweiligen Klasse an der ideellen ",
    "Gesamtfläche. Die Werte dieser Zeile summieren sich über alle Klassen zu ",
    "100 %."))
notes <- c(notes, paste0(
  "Anz. Pkte.: Anzahl der Inventurpunkte, auf denen die jeweilige Gruppe ",
  "vertreten ist. Die Summe über die Tabelle kann von der oben angegebenen ",
  "Gesamtzahl der Inventurpunkte abweichen, weil nicht auf jedem Inventurpunkt ",
  "Bäume vorkommen, die den Auswahlkriterien dieser Tabelle entsprechen."))

# Emitted as raw LaTeX: use real environments throughout. A bare "{ ... }"
# grouping is NOT recognised as LaTeX by pandoc and would leak into the text.
cat("\n\\vspace{0.8em}\n\\begin{footnotesize}\n")
cat("\\textbf{Erläuterungen}\n")
cat("\\begin{itemize}\\setlength{\\itemsep}{0pt}\\setlength{\\parskip}{0pt}",
    "\\setlength{\\topsep}{2pt}\n", sep = "")
for (nt in notes) cat("\\item ", esc(nt), "\n", sep = "")
cat("\\end{itemize}\n\\end{footnotesize}\n")
```
